summary: Round-3 final re-verify. My round-2 P1 (deactivated human could deliver the 2nd dual-control signature / reject on POST /api/rights/change-requests/:id/{approve,reject}) is genuinely FIXED: assertApproverIsHuman now carries AND ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL in its WHERE (fail-closed 403, no oracle), moved allowlist -> AUTHORITY_RESOLVERS, and a live-PG regression (rights-change-requests-deactivated-approver.db.test.ts, 4/4) drives the REAL routes proving deactivated approve/reject on both grant and role_assignment = 403 with confirmed2_by staying NULL, while an ACTIVE distinct human still gets 200 (INV-3 no over-block). Agent path unaffected (predicate is a no-op for agents -> row still returned -> DC-3 kind-check fires AGENT_NOT_ALLOWED, correct code, verified by reasoning + unchanged kind check). My 3 round-2 scan bypasses (window-8 / alias / JOIN) are CLOSED and I re-broke them RED against the LIVE gate in a faithful fakeroot. The builder's own re-inventory surfaced and fixed an 8th live authority path — binding.ts:checkRole (process_designer membership -> 403) now carries e.ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL (correct alias) + registered; three genuinely-non-authority lookups (getHoldersForRole, getRoleAssignmentOrgScopesForEmployee, grant-propose PROPOSAL_AGENT) added to the allowlist with sound reasons. Manual full scan of all 42 slug-lookups in src/db+src/http (coordinator ask г): every employee-table actor lookup sits inside a FROM|JOIN choros.employee window and maps to a registered/allowlisted function — NO false negatives in the current tree; the non-employee ones (registry_def/role/tenant/application) are correctly out of scope. Gate live + self-test green on BSD awk (macOS) AND mawk 1.3.4 (postgres:16). All requested gates pass. Residual: the accounting scan is still a HEURISTIC — three implausible-styling bypasses remain (slug 26+ lines past FROM; backtick string-concat; a `;` inside a string literal before the slug) — but none exist in the tree, all require a deliberately-odd query that ALSO forgets the predicate, and the real control is the runtime predicate (proven by db tests). Non-blocking P3. Nothing blocks merge.

coordinator_checks.a_agent_path_ordering: OK — the predicate does not give an active agent a spurious 403 before the kind-check. Agents have deactivated_at permanently NULL (migration 125 is human-only; agent_card has no deactivation column — actor-authority-gate.ts header), so an agent's employee row is still RETURNED by the predicate-carrying SELECT, then rows[0].kind !== 'human' throws AGENT_NOT_ALLOWED. A deactivated HUMAN yields zero rows -> 403 FORBIDDEN (indistinguishable from not-found, no oracle). No agent-deactivation scenario exists.
coordinator_checks.b_checkRole_alias_and_active_pass: OK — the predicate is written e.${ACTOR_ACTIVE_SQL} = e.deactivated_at IS NULL, correctly qualified to the joined employee alias e (role_assignment ra / role r / employee e; deactivated_at exists only on employee, so no ambiguity). A legitimate ACTIVE process_designer has e.deactivated_at NULL -> counted -> passes (no over-block). binding unit tests (binding-owner-bypass 4, binding-get-layout 4, floor1-editor 69) all green; tsc clean.
coordinator_checks.c_gates_and_bypasses: gate live RC=0 (FF-0662-1 7/7, FF-0662-2 clean), self-test RC=0 (now embeds judge attacks a/b + bypasses d/e/f + N-1), both re-run green on Linux mawk. My 3 round-2 bypasses replayed against the live gate: all RC=1 (caught). db regress 4/4. dual-control-isolation / anti-case-lock / single-resolver / grant-resolver-isolation / frozen-checks-immutable all PASS.

Employee-table actor lookups (grants-dao 259/445/456/576, org 222/323/538/740/793/816, report-page 274, rights-intents 1203, rights-change-requests 189, binding 214, sod-dao 396, substitution-dao 204/292, rights-sod 274, rights-overview 211, assistant 1290/1783, solution-bundles 113, pdp-explain 120, grant-propose 365) are ALL within a FROM|JOIN choros.employee window and ALL registered or allowlisted (org.ts:323 confirmed inside resolveActorTenant, allowlisted). The rest resolve registry_def / role / tenant / application (not employee) and are correctly uncounted. No un-gated authority lookup hides past the window in the current tree.

non_blocking.title: Accounting scan remains a heuristic — three implausible-styling bypasses persist (no live instance)
non_blocking.where: ci/checks/actor-authority-deactivation-gate.sh count_lookups_in_file :299-314 (EMP_WINDOW=25; early-close on any backtick or ';' on a line :310).
non_blocking.evidence: Empirically, each keeps the live gate GREEN with an un-gated authority lookup: (g) slug=$ placed 26+ lines after FROM choros.employee (beyond window=25); (h) a backtick string-concatenation between FROM and the slug (early-close on backtick); (i) a semicolon INSIDE a string literal (e.g. e.note = 'x;y') on a line before the slug (early-close treats any ';' as a statement terminator). None occur in the current tree (verified by the full manual scan); each needs a deliberately-unusual query that ALSO omits the predicate.
non_blocking.impact: Inherent limit of a grep/awk static scan — substantially narrower than round 2 (which missed plain alias/JOIN/9-line styles). The security guarantee is delivered by the RUNTIME predicates in the 7 registered resolvers (proven by db regression), with the scan as anti-forgetting defense-in-depth. Realistic forgetting (a plainly-written new authority lookup) is caught. ADR already frames the scan as a heuristic.
non_blocking.suggest: Optional hardening, not required for merge: only treat ';' as a terminator when it is the last non-space char on the line (ignore in-string semicolons); raise/remove EMP_WINDOW and instead bound by the closing backtick of the same template literal; add g/h/i as self-test probes to prevent silent regression of these edges.
